title: upgrade-attn-flashattnv2-rope-fused-kv-batching-scheduling
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Upgrade the attention kernels to the FlashAttentionV2 variant with fused rotational/rope ops and improved KV-cache handling to reduce latency and increase throughput for long-context workloads. This PR combines kernel updates, a small scheduler improvement to favor KV-friendly micro-batching, and a KV-cache API tweak to enable continuous batching without cache thrashing.

Summary of changes: - Integrate upstream FlashAttentionV2 kernels with our fused-rope/rotary patchset and apply Redwood-specific memory layout optimizations. - Add optional fused rotary/rope codepath toggles to select depending on model config (rotary vs rope). - Modify runtime scheduler to detect high-KV hit-rate traffic and switch to a KV-prefetch micro-batching policy that groups requests by prefix similarity. - Improve KV cache eviction heuristics to keep longer-lived prefixes for long-context streaming. - Add unit and e2e tests + perf harness entries and benchmarks for base/streaming/long-context scenarios.

Benchmarks: Measured on p4d.24xlarge and RTX A6000 staging clusters. Representative results: - 32k context throughput (tokens/sec) improved: +1.8x average for decoder-only models on 4x A100 equivalent. - Median next-token latency at 8k context: -28% on p4d cluster. - Streaming tail latency (95th) improved by ~22% with KV-prefetch micro-batching. - Memory use per request reduced ~12% on average due to fused op kernel packing. Bench run details in perf-canary under canary/372800-run1.tar.gz (artifact).

Compatibility and safety: - The fused rope/rotary path is off by default for models flagged as unknown; model onboarding adds a small metadata flag for rotary vs rope. - Fall back to previous attention kernels on unsupported GPUs or when JIT compilation fails. - No public API changes; runtime flags: REDWOOD_USE_FLASHATTV2 (auto) and REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH_THRESHOLD (int).

Testing: - Added unit tests for attention kernel selection logic and fused-op correctness across rotary/rope inputs. - e2e tests for continuous batching with synthetic workloads and playback of real traffic traces from the canary environment. - CI: linux-gpu build, unit tests, integration tests. Local perf harness scripts included.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout with canary group of internal clusters, monitor token-level latency+cost dashboards and quality regressions using existing eval prompt suites. If any regression >2% in accuracy/LL or >15% latency increase, feature gates trigger automatic rollback.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel integration and unit tests
- [x] Scheduler & KV-cache heuristics implemented
- [x] Perf benchmarks added
- [x] Feature flagging & safe-fallbacks
- [x] Docs & release notes draft

Related: ENG-1428 (attention kernel upgrades), ENG-1499 (continuous batching scheduling), SUP-8812 (customer case reporting tail latency at 16k contexts).
